extraction.name: OpenBookQA
extraction.description: A dataset for open book question answering consisting of about 6,000 4-way multiple-choice questions, each associated with one core fact from a book of 1326 elementary science facts, requiring combination with additional common knowledge.
extraction.creator: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were created through a multi-stage crowdsourcing pipeline starting from a set of core science facts, where workers generated a second common fact, wrote multiple-choice questions, passed automatic hardness checks, were validated by additional crowd workers for answerability, had answer choices shuffled, and Dev/Test were further filtered by an in-house expert.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Experiments, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: A subset of the WorldTree corpus consisting of 1326 central elementary science facts, plus crowdsourced second facts collected during question generation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset construction included filtering WorldTree facts to those general enough for multiple situations, automatic checks on question format and answer choice uniformity, automatic hardness filtering against IR and association solvers, answerability filtering by crowd workers, random shuffling of answer choices, and expert filtering for Dev and Test.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers were shown a science fact, asked to think of a second common fact, combine them into a valid assertion, convert it into a question-answer pair, extend it into a 4-way multiple-choice question, and then separate crowd workers answered the question to verify answerability; Dev and Test were additionally filtered by an in-house expert.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A question was kept only if at least 4 of 5 crowd workers answered it correctly; the paper also analyzes human accuracy estimation using these annotations and notes that the second facts were often incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers from North America with a masters-level qualification
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes inevitable human bias in the crowdsourced dataset, including answer choice position bias and artifacts exploitable by simple neural baselines.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The open book facts alone are generally insufficient; the auxiliary second facts are noisy and should not be treated as gold; some questions do not actually require the original science fact; and even with oracle facts, reasoning remains challenging.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for open book question answering research, with Train/Dev/Test splits and intermediate supervision via the associated core fact for Train and Dev questions.

name.evidence: we present a new kind of question answering dataset, OpenBookQA

description.evidence: The OpenBookQA dataset consists of about 6,000 4-way multiple-choice questions, each associated with one core fact from a “book” F of 1326 such facts, and an auxiliary set K of about 6000 additional facts.

url.evidence: The dataset and the code for the models are available at http://data.allenai.org/OpenBookQA .

creator.evidence: Todor Mihaylovzand Peter Clarkyand Tushar Khotyand Ashish Sabharwaly

publisher.evidence: yAllen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Seattle, WA, U.S.A.

inLanguage.evidence: We present a new kind of question answering dataset, OpenBookQA

isLiveDataset.evidence: OpenBookQA consists of 5957 questions, with 4957/500/500 in the Train/Dev/Test splits.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The questions were created via a multi-stage crowdsourcing and partial expert filtering process, discussed in Section 3.1.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We used a multi-stage process starting with F, using crowd-sourcing to generate (noisy) questions based on F, using an automatic filter to ensure hardness for retrieval and association based systems, using a crowd filter to ensure answerability by a lay person, and further using an expert filter to ensure higher quality in Dev and Test sets.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: For F, we use a subset of the WorldTree corpus which Jansen et al. (2018) have analyzed for sufficiency for elementary level science.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We further filter them down to 1326 that appear general enough to be applicable to multiple situations.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: A crowd-worker5 w is shown a random science fact f from the set F.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We used Amazon Mechnical Turk, with workers from North America and with a ‘masters’ level qualification.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: If at least 4 out of 5 workers answer qmc correctly, it is deemed answerable and the process continues.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Question qmc is then shown to 5 new crowd-workers, who are asked to answer it.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: We used Amazon Mechnical Turk, with workers from North America and with a ‘masters’ level qualification.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: These highlight inevitable human bias in any crowdsourced dataset, increasing performance on OpenBookQA to 48%.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We emphasize that K should not be viewed as ‘gold’ additional facts, or as a substitute for broad common knowledge.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: To encourage further research on this new task, for each Train and Dev question q, OpenBookQA also includes f as intermediate supervision signal, which may be viewed as a partial explanation for q.
